passage: Playroom note, Wednesday. Tarun jammed the square block against the round hole and pounded it with a flat palm over and over. The palm turned pink and tears began, but the block stayed on top. I sat down beside Tarun, held the square and the circle side by side, and said, "Different." Tarun stared, then sniffed and picked up the circle piece instead. Tomorrow I will set the shapes out one by one. Kalyani

qa.q: What did Tarun pound with a flat palm?
qa.a: Tarun pounded the square block against the round hole.

qa.q: What was Tarun feeling when the tears began?
qa.a: Tarun was frustrated and upset, because all the effort was getting nowhere.

qa.q: What different approach could Tarun try, and why?
qa.a: Tarun could look for the hole that has the same shape as the block, because pushing harder cannot change the shape of the piece.

qa.q: How does Kalyani see Tarun's pounding?
qa.a: Kalyani sees hard effort that is going nowhere, so Kalyani sits down and shows the two shapes side by side rather than telling Tarun to stop.

grounding: A toddler hammers a square block on a round hole with a palm, using force that does not change the block's shape.

passage: In the courtyard of the house near Sitapur, Vikas sat with the wooden shape board his uncle had made. The square block wouldn't go into the round hole. He smacked it with his palm. Smack. Smack. Smack. His sister Disha, drawing water at the handpump, called, "Vikas, that's the wrong hole!" He smacked harder, face red, the block hopping on the rim and never sinking in.

qa.q: What was Disha doing at the handpump?
What was Vikas feeling as he smacked harder?
qa.a: He was frustrated and stubborn, sure that more force would push the block in.

qa.q: What else could Vikas try instead of smacking?
qa.a: He could try the block in the other holes or turn to Disha for help, because hitting harder does not change the block's shape.

qa.q: How does the smacking look to Disha?
qa.a: Disha sees clearly that he has the wrong hole and is a little amused and a little exasperated that he won't listen.

grounding: A toddler hammers a square block on a round hole with his palm, putting in effort that cannot change the fit.

passage: Sami knelt on the living-room carpet in Tunis, a blue square block pressed to the round hole of the shape box. Thump went his palm. Thump. Thump. His father, Siddiq, looked up from folding towels. "Strong hands!" Sami thumped harder, lips pressed together. The block stayed on top, not budging. His palm turned pink. He thumped once more, then shoved the whole box.

qa.q: What was Siddiq doing when he looked up?
What was Sami feeling when he shoved the whole box?
qa.a: He was angry and frustrated after all his thumping failed.

qa.q: Which approach would suit Sami better?
qa.a: Trying the block in other holes or turning it to match, since force alone can't change a square into a circle.

qa.q: How might Siddiq see the thumping?
qa.a: Siddiq first sees effort and praises it, then may realise Sami needs a nudge toward the square hole instead.

grounding: A toddler hits a square block on the round hole again and again, and the force changes nothing.
